the_signal.headline: RPA dies—workflow automation with native async APIs wins at scale
the_signal.body: n8n's comparison of RPA vs. workflow automation exposes a hard truth: traditional RPA can't handle event-driven architectures or async request-response decoupling that production AI systems demand. If you're building GTM automation that coordinates multiple agents across async boundaries, you need native async API support, not RPA bots that can't reason about state or timing. This isn't theoretical—it's the difference between deployable and fragile.

thread_of_day.title: Authentication & Authorization Patterns in Production AI Workflows
thread_of_day.takeaway: API key vs. token tradeoffs matter more in multi-agent systems where you're rotating credentials between LLM calls, database writes, and third-party webhooks—token-based auth with expiry windows beats static keys for security at scale.

quote.text: We don't know how much a token really costs. They are subsidized by big tech and most AI providers are operating at a loss.
quote.source: n8n Blog—Token prices won't increase if you host your own LLMs

whats_moving.topic: Async API architecture for AI workflows
whats_moving.context: n8n is pushing async-first patterns hard; decoupling request/response is now table-stakes for scaling multi-agent orchestration without blocking.
The subsidy thesis is hardening—if token prices rise post-funding, self-hosting margin advantage becomes real; this justifies engineering spend on deployment infrastructure now.
n8n's alternative comparison signals market pressure; vendors are being forced to compete on self-hosting, observability, and governance—not just features.

act_on_this: Audit your current AI automation stack: if you're using RPA or webhook-based choreography for multi-agent flows, migrate to an event-driven workflow platform (n8n, Make, or self-hosted) with native async API support before Q4. RPA will fail under coordination load.
